name: Nuclear plant safety
summary: Zaporizhzhia's off-site power remains fragile as strikes on Ukraine's grid continue
state: The Zaporizhzhia plant has lost all off-site power more than 20 times during the war, according to IAEA counts (News on AIR), and repairs to its lines have been repeatedly delayed by fighting. Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy system continued into 7 Nov (Ukrinform). No damage to safety systems or radiological release had been reported as of 7 Nov.
for_you: Follow official guidance from the IAEA and national authorities; no protective action is advised.
rubric_hit: Fragile off-site power, IAEA concern = Watch; no safety-system damage (Alert)

sources.title: News on AIR — IAEA says Zaporizhzhia loses off-site power for 21st time
Ukrinform — Ukrainian forces neutralise 94 of 128 Russian drones overnight

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
